q: My studio only runs 1 x prenatal class a week and my lift classes don’t accept pregnant women 😭 I’m struggling with home workouts on YouTube
cx: A previously very active London woman in her second trimester looking for a prenatal trainer.

q: it’s so incredibly frustrating that most studios in London tend to hold their prenatal classes during weekdays in the morning - someone needs to fill this gap in the market asap!
cx: Working pregnant woman can't attend daytime prenatal classes.

q: I feel so behind, and every time I try to research something, I end up even more confused. I spend hours scrolling, comparing products, reading reviews and saving things, but never actually buying anything.
cx: At 27 weeks with her first, UK-based, she has bought almost nothing.

q: Sometimes I genuinely think our grandmothers had it easier when there were only one or two options available. 😂
cx: On the number of baby product choices.

q:
You name it, Facebook has advertised it to me.

And of course, my husband thinks we should buy ALL of them. 😄
cx: Feeding gadgets advertised to her, and her husband's view.

q: So how on earth am I supposed to decide which feeding equipment to buy when I don’t even know how I’ll feed my baby?
cx: Unsure whether she will breastfeed, so unsure what to buy.

q: I’m honestly starting to feel like I’m drowning in information. Every product claims to be essential, every brand claims to be the best, and every parent seems to have a different opinion.
cx: How baby-product research feels at 27 weeks.

q: Currently 30 weeks pregnant and attending NCT antenatal classes. I had hoped to make friends and make connections during this but unfortunately with the group I am in I just haven’t managed to.
cx: She paid for NCT classes partly to make friends; it hasn't happened.

q: I worry I will struggle during maternity leave when my other friends are in full time work and don’t live in my area.
cx: Her fear of isolation once the baby comes.

q: If you did buy and use one, did it feel work it to drop $75-100 on? At how many weeks did it start working for you?
cx: First pregnancy; weighing a home fetal heart monitor to settle her worries.
r: anxiety in unit; home monitoring device

q: I have not hit my deductible yet so (so close omg) I’d have to pay for it, but I’ve heard really mixed opinions on doing it
cx: At 12 weeks deciding whether to pay for NIPT before meeting her deductible.

q: they presented me with a contract that required at least have of the full amount they are asking for that would cover subsequent visits and the doctor delivering at the hospital.
cx: Her US obstetric practice asks for prepayment before her anatomy scan.

q: for me it’s a little stressful and feels like I’m pressured to stick to one OBGYN even though I want to see my other option and make sure I’m making a good decision.
cx: The prepayment contract pressures her before she has chosen her doctor.

q: I usually just go to Primark and get some granny knickers then pop into boots and get their own brand maternity pads.
cx: Pregnant with her fourth, she has always assembled her own postpartum supplies cheaply.

q: Part of me really wants one but it seems like a lot of money for what could essentially be a bit of a gimmick!
cx: Offered a ready-made postpartum kit as a gift; she may ask for a voucher instead.

q: We have tried everything recommended by the midwives, paediatrician and the GP but nothing is working.
cx: UK parent of a 3-week-old with a worsening nappy rash, hunting a discontinued cream.

q: I planned for a vaginal delivery buying tucks pads, dermaplast, and pad ice packs but I ended up having an unplanned c section. I even bought a sitz bath.
cx: First-time mother listing postpartum supplies she bought and never needed.

q: I ended up buying a pump because I wanted to primarily pump but I hate the sensation of pumping so it was a waste of money to include all the milk storage bags, nipple covers, and nipple ice packs.
cx: Feeding supplies bought before the birth that went unused.

q: Bottles are so expensive too. We bought the dr.browns full set with bottle warmer and everything. I heard such great reviews on dr.browns and those bottles don’t work for my newborn.
cx: A well-reviewed bottle set that didn't suit her baby.

q: 😭 it’s always the worst when you total the amount wasted
cx: Reacting to others' lists of unused baby purchases.

q: I'm 40+4 currently and I'm my last ditch attempts of 'preparing'.
cx: Past her due date, she is buying nursing bras.

q: I don't want to spend $$ on one that fits now/soon but might be completely wrong in a few weeks time.
cx: Timing a nursing-bra purchase around body changes.

q: After insurance my bill is $800 and they refuse to honor the cash price quoted by my ob because it already went through insurance.
cx: A US NIPT bill after insurance, far above the cash price quoted.

q: What’s still ridiculous is that the first guy I spoke to was being intentionally obtuse and didn’t say this was a possibility at all 🙃
cx: After a second call, the lab bill dropped to about the cash price.

q: I’m looking at strollers that aren’t super expensive but worth it. Currently looking at Hagaday 2 in 1 stroller ($169 on Amazon currently) has anyone used it?
cx: 16 days postpartum, shopping for a light, cheap stroller.

q: First time mom here and my employer offers doula coverage (they pay 70% of fee). Since that’s a majority of the cost, I am very interested in getting one for birth or postpartum. Maybe even both!
cx: An employer benefit covers most of a doula's fee; she is unsure what doulas do.

q: However, I don’t fully understand what they do and if it’s truly worth it. While I wouldn’t have to pay much, that money could be used elsewhere.
cx: Even subsidised, she questions a doula's value.

q: This is my husband’s first child as well and both of our parents’ first grandchild. There is A LOT we don’t know
cx: No one in either family has done this before.

q: My employer also offers online birthing classes so if you think that is more worth it, please let me know.
cx: Weighing an employer-funded online birth class against a doula.

q: I spent so much time researching baby products before my baby was born, so figured I’d share one that actually lived up to the expectations!!
cx: A simple non-wifi baby monitor she rebought the night it broke.

q: just found out I’m pregnant ❤️ ❤️ but I’m already feeling overwhelmed trying to set up my daily prenatal routine.
cx: Newly pregnant, comparing prenatal vitamin formulations; post reads partly like brand promotion.

q: I'm trying to sort out the setup now, before the sleep deprivation hits.
cx: Second baby due when her daughter is 18-19 months; deciding on a double pram.

q: The other thing on my mind is that I might end up with a C-section. I'm wondering how that changes things: carrying a newborn in the early weeks, lifting a toddler into a seat, pushing a heavy double up a curb…
cx: Planning the newborn weeks with a toddler around a possible surgical birth.

q: She does half up front and the remainder around 36 weeks. I personally think it’s worth it??? But I’m new to all this and idk if it’s a high price.
cx: Weighing a $3,000 doula package recommended by a coworker and her OB.

q: She’s well known and trusted by hospital staff, my coworker loved having her for both pregnancies.
cx: What tips her towards the $3,000 doula.

q: However, it is $80 (with shipping and taxes) and as we are already spending so much on baby stuff, I don’t want to spend that much on something I might look back on as totally unnecessary.
cx: First-time mother tempted by a designer birthing gown.

q: I would just sway my head and either say, “My baby is coming,” “Help me God,” or “Thank you God” while I squeezed my birth comb during contractions.
cx: Day-of birth story from a first-time mother with a disability; what she did on the drive in.

q: I originally was very against pushing on my back and had hands and knees pushing or side lying pushing on my birth plan, but it felt right at the moment.
cx: How her birth plan changed in the moment.

q: Overall it was great experience! I was so scared to give birth unmedicated but it was very empowering. My husband said it was the most impressive thing I’ve ever done and I really appreciated his support.
cx: Her feelings after the birth and what her husband said.

q: To sum up, even though I was scared of reactions, I’m SO happy I advocated for myself and followed through. You don’t realize how bad you feel until you get some relief.
cx: Second pregnancy; she pushed past dismissive care to get treated for exhaustion.
r: medical treatment; past birth complication in unit

q: I was feeling extreme fatigue, heart palpitations, anxiety, and so much more that I just chalked up to pregnancy because my OB said it was.
cx: Her symptoms were waved off as normal pregnancy.

q: I vividly remember being a few days postpartum and scrolling through this and other reddit feeds, searching for two types of stories - other people who were also struggling and parents who had positive things to share.
cx: Seven months on, recalling what she searched for in the first days home.

q: It is ok if you do not feel overwhelming love the second your baby comes out of you. I cared about my son immediately and I always wanted the best for him. But I did not truly feel a deeper sense of love until he was two months old.
cx: What she wants new mothers to hear about the first weeks.

q: I remember being 2 weeks postpartum and looking at our wedding pictures in tears, thinking "what did we do!". It is certainly difficult to feel that way - I felt soooo guilty - but it can be totally normal!
cx: A scene from her second week home.

q: No one can prepare you for what the lack of sleep actually feels like. And I say this as someone who does well with little sleep and is a morning person.
cx: On whether newborn sleep loss can be prepared for.

q: I have driven myself absolutely insane and exhausted from googling/reddit-ing/chat gpt-ing every symptom and every food to see if it is safe for pregnancy.
cx: At 28 weeks with her first, in France, describing months of checking everything online.

q: I also feel like the constant access to information through social media/ the internet is extremely detrimental to someone with an anxious thought pattern.
cx: What she concluded after her doctor reassured her.

q: I felt like I finally realized that I am allowed to simply enjoy this period of my life.
cx: Turning point after an appointment where she cried with relief.

q: My plan was to always get the epidural but I really wanted to experience labor. Well I did. And it was insanity.
cx: Second birth, under a day old; the epidural came too late.

q: I was SCREAMING at this point in pain and for relief, crying that I didn’t want to do it this way, I never wanted to labor unmedicated.
cx: The moment labour went faster than she expected.

q: All of this to say, it was the most insane experience of my life. It hurt so bad, I genuinely don’t know how I survived. But I did. And I feel really fucking cool because of it.
cx: How she felt the day after an unplanned unmedicated birth.

q: I was so scared that the pain and suffering was going inhibit my ability to push him out. I genuinely can’t believe I made it through.
cx: Her fear during the last stage of labour.
